headline: Broad Iran/Hormuz risk-off session: KSE-100 opened flat but sold off through the day as Iran said it will declare a new exclusion zone near the Strait of Hormuz, closing 172,642.16 (-993.91pts, -0.57%) with Brent near a seven-week high (~$99). The move was market-wide, not stock-specific — every portfolio holding drifted down a little (biggest: AVN -4.0%, MUGHAL -3.4%, SEARL -3.0%), none crossed the 5% single-name trigger, so no notification went out today. Holdings synced mid-review from off-app buys: MZNPETF 25,000→32,000 sh (avg 18.93→18.67), MIIETF 10,000→13,000 sh (avg 16.62→16.59), EFERT 2,800→3,000 sh (avg 197.97→196.99) — the two ETF top-ups landed right in their ADD zones (nice execution); the small EFERT add came in a bit above its WATCH-tier entry (~183 vs 174) but the amount is minor. Portfolio value ~Rs 10.26M, P/L ~+Rs 0.8K (+0.01% on cost) — essentially breakeven: the broad-based dip plus the new EFERT/MZNPETF lots being slightly underwater at today's prices offset each other. Drawdown from the Jan 23 ATH (189,556) widened again to ~8.9% (from ~8.4% Friday/Monday) — still short of the 10% dry-powder trigger but closing in faster than usual given two straight geopolitically-driven red sessions. AVN's EXIT call remains unexecuted (24,500 shares still held, 10 reviews running now) — no new company news since the Aug 28 filing. DRAP pricing-formula story unchanged: pharma industry associations reiterated public opposition (Sep 4 article) but nothing enacted yet — GLAXO/SEARL stance unchanged (HOLD, watch into Q4). Entry levels reassessed this review: no changes warranted — today's move is news-driven, not a break of monthly support. Housekeeping: git connectivity to github.com timed out again early in this run (raw.githubusercontent.com/api.github.com stayed reachable throughout — isolated to the git endpoint) and had not recovered by the time this review's price/action content was finalized; push retried once holdings were synced.
market: KSE-100 closed 172,642.16 Tue Sep 8, down 993.91pts (-0.57%), extending Monday's 1,692.75pt drop — two consecutive red sessions on escalating US-Iran tensions. Iran's Supreme National Security Council said Tehran plans to announce a maritime exclusion zone near the Strait of Hormuz restricting vessel transit without Iranian permission; Brent crude traded near a seven-week high (~$99/bbl), stoking Pakistan's import-bill/current-account worries. The selloff was broad-based across the index (banks, cement, autos, E&Ps) rather than concentrated in any single sector holding the portfolio owns. Drawdown from the Jan 23 ATH (189,556) is now ~8.92%, up from ~8.4% Monday — still below the 10% line that would justify shifting the AICF/MICF cash reserve into MZNPETF/MIIETF, but the gap has narrowed roughly 1.3 points in two sessions; worth checking daily while Hormuz tensions stay elevated. SBP holds at 11.5%; next MPC meeting is Sep 14, 2026 (6 days away, no change expected). No fresh SBP reserves figure found this review — last known ~$17.12B (week of Aug 28), not reconfirmed today. DRAP drug-pricing review: pharma industry associations reiterated public opposition to the proposed formula/Hardship Policy/Policy Board changes (Sep 4 coverage); nothing enacted yet — still a sector-wide watch item, not a GLAXO/SEARL-specific fundamental break; HOLD stance unchanged for both, watch into Q4. EFERT — no material news since the Q2 briefing; the Rs2/share record some data providers list against a Sep 3 pay date is still the same interim already credited back on May 13, 2026 (stale/duplicated third-party record) — no new dividend event, WATCH/re-evaluate-at-Q3 stance unchanged. AVN — no new company announcements since the Aug 28 H1/Q2 FY26 loss filing; EXIT call unexecuted through 10 reviews now. Fatima Fertilizer's H1 2026 results (already covered last review: profit +20.7% YoY) remain the only fresh company filing found this week; no update for Mughal or Meezan Bank beyond routine price action. DATA QUALITY: stock prices refreshed normally (mid-session snapshot ~08:39 UTC / 13:39 PKT, ahead of the ~15:30 PKT close). Fund NAVs (funds_updated: Aug 13) are now 26 days stale — the MUFAP scraper issue remains unresolved; ~28% of portfolio value (all 7 funds) is still being priced off a nearly month-old NAV snapshot, a growing blind spot needing a real fix.

actions.title: Avanceon — thesis still broken, EXIT call unexecuted through 10 reviews
actions.detail: No new news since the Aug 28 H1/Q2 FY26 filing: consolidated H1 2026 revenue grew +34% YoY but the company swung from a Rs 168M profit to a Rs 260M NET LOSS (EPS -Rs 0.62 vs +Rs 0.38); Q2 alone the loss widened to Rs 317M. No dividend declared. Admin/selling expenses up 45% YoY outpaced revenue growth, and a one-off 'other income' cushion from last year (Rs 162M) collapsed to Rs 77M this year, exposing weak core operating economics — real, board-confirmed deterioration, not a rumor. Now Rs 28.80 (-36.1% on cost), down another ~4% today in the broad selloff. No earnings catalyst pending before Q3; there's no reason left to keep waiting. The Aug 25 EXIT call is unexecuted through 10 reviews now — recommend selling the entire position at market.

These are accumulation guides, not precise buy/sell signals — verify with your broker.
